newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines opposes listing of Boulevard shares.
newsitem.headline: Philippines opposes listing of Boulevard shares.

text.p: The Philippines' Presidential Commission on Good Government (PCGG) is opposing the listing of Boulevard Properties Holdings Inc's (BHI) shares next Monday, according to documents submitted to the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) on Thursday.
Boulevard has sold 500 million of its shares to the public at one peso per share.
The PCGG said Boulevard sourced 250 million pesos of its equity from advances made through borrowings from companies whose funds, in turn, came from sequestered companies.
The commission is the custodian of sequestered assets of former strongman Ferdinand Marcos and his business associates.
PCGG Commissioner Herminio Mendoza said Silahis International Hotel and Puerto Azual Land Inc, which have pending court cases involving sequestered shares, are the two of Boulevard's benefactors.
"We urge that your office adopt the necessary measure for the protection of the government as well as the buying public," Mendoza said in his letter.
However, Boulevard vice chairman Lorenzo Tanada III said the bourse should disregard the opposition since it was filed long after the period to contest its application had expired.
The basis for the opposition is not grounds for preventing the list and borrowings by the company were ordinary business transactions which had been disclosed to the exchange, he added.
